data.title: Zymeworks Presents New Phase 1 Data for Folate Receptor Alpha-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugate ZW191 at ESMO Congress 2026
data.description:
• ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha (FRα) expression levels
  • Confirmed objective response rates (cORR) of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
  • Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups
  • Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration
  • Conference call with Zymeworks management on October 27 at 8:30 am Eastern Time (ET)

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zymeworks Inc. (Nasdaq: ZYME), a biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets while developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics, today presented new clinical data from the randomized dose-optimization portion of its ongoing Phase 1 study evaluating ZW191, a FRα-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain.

The presentation highlights compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), including patients with high-grade serous disease across all levels of FRα expression. The results demonstrate compelling response rates, durability and a favorable tolerability profile, particularly at the 6.4 mg/kg dose, further supporting the potential of ZW191 to address limitations of currently available FRα-targeted therapies and expand treatment opportunities for patients with ovarian cancer.

“We are highly encouraged by these results, which further demonstrate the differentiated clinical profile of ZW191 and its potential to deliver meaningful benefit to patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer,” said Sabeen Mekan, M.D., Senior Vice President and Chief Medical Officer, Zymeworks. “The robust response rates observed at both doses, including meaningful activity in patients with low or negative FRα expression, reinforce the potential of ZW191 to benefit a broader patient population. Importantly, the encouraging durability of responses and favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, provide valuable insights to guide dose selection and the next stage of clinical development.”

The analysis included efficacy and safety data from 80 patients with PROC randomized to receive ZW191 at 6.4 mg/kg (n=37) or 9.6 mg/kg (n=43) every three weeks, as of the September 10, 2026 data cutoff date. Patients were heavily pretreated, having received a median of four prior lines of therapy, with 45% receiving five or more prior lines. Median follow-up was seven months. FRα expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry and categorized as low/negative (0%–24%), intermediate (25%–74%) or high (75%–100%) based on the percentage of tumor cells with 2+ or 3+ staining intensity.

Key Findings

Among response-evaluable patients with high-grade serous PROC, ZW191 demonstrated a cORR of 64.5% at 6.4 mg/kg and 55.3% at 9.6 mg/kg, with disease control rates of 100% and 92.1%, respectively. These findings demonstrate compelling anti-tumor activity at both doses in a heavily pretreated patient population.

ZW191 demonstrated meaningful anti-tumor activity across FRα expression in patients with high-grade serous PROC. Confirmed objective response rates were 69.2% in patients with high FRα expression, 50.0% in patients with intermediate FRα expression and 55.0% in patients with low or negative FRα expression. These findings support the potential of ZW191 to show improved efficacy than existing FRα targeted therapies in FRα high population and meaningfully benefit patients with lower expression who may not be eligible for currently approved FRα targeting therapies.

Responses to ZW191 were deep and durable, with median duration of response not yet reached at either dose. Six-month progression-free survival (PFS) was 61% in both groups, while median PFS was 7.9 months at 6.4 mg/kg and 9.8 months at 9.6 mg/kg in patients with high-grade serous PROC. At the time of data cutoff, 45% of patients remained on treatment, and PFS data continue to mature, especially at 6.4 mg/kg.

ZW191 continued to demonstrate a favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22% of patients receiving 6.4 mg/kg compared with 44% at 9.6 mg/kg. Treatment-emergent adverse events leading to dose reductions occurred in 5% and 33% of patients, respectively, while discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in 14% and 19%. No deaths due to treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in either treatment group. The overall safety profile was manageable and supports continued clinical development.

“These results are particularly promising for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer who have exhausted available treatment options,” said Jung-Yun Lee, M.D., Ph.D., Yonsei Cancer Center and Severance Hospital, Seoul, Republic of South Korea, and primary investigator who presented the results at ESMO 2026. “We observed substantial anti-tumor activity in patients who had received multiple prior therapies, including meaningful responses across high, intermediate and low or negative FRα expression levels. The encouraging durability of responses, together with the favorable safety profile observed at the lower dose, suggests ZW191 has the potential to become an important new treatment option for patients with this difficult-to-treat disease.”

The findings demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity across the 6.4 mg/kg and 9.6 mg/kg dose levels, with a more favorable tolerability profile at 6.4 mg/kg. These results will inform optimal dose selection for further clinical development.

ZW191's differentiated profile, including its novel FRα-targeting antibody, proprietary topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, ZD06519, and high drug-to-antibody ratio, supports its potential to address key limitations of existing therapies and broaden the applicability of FRα-targeted treatment approaches.

The presentation will be available on Zymeworks’ website at www.zymeworks.com/publications/.

Investor Call Details

Zymeworks invites investors and the general public to view and listen to a live webcast of its conference call with investment analysts at 8:30 am ET on October 27, 2026.

Dial-in details and webcast link are available on Zymeworks’ website at https://ir.zymeworks.com/events-and-presentations. A webcast replay of the call will be available on the Zymeworks website within 24 hours following the conclusion of the live call and will be archived for a limited period.

About ZW191

ZW191 is an antibody-drug conjugate engineered to target a protein called folate receptor-⍺ found in ~75% of high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas,1 over 50% of endometrial cancers,2,3 and ~70% of lung adenocarcinomas4. ZW191’s differentiated design strongly supports its ability to internalize into FR⍺-expressing cells with the potential to release bystander active topoisomerase-1 inhibitor (ZD06519), a novel proprietary payload developed by Zymeworks to kill tumor cells.

The Company has engaged MTS Healthcare to evaluate strategic partnering opportunities to fund further development for ZW191 with the objective of maximizing long-term value.

About Zymeworks Inc.

Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies.

Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. These capabilities, together with Zymeworks’ integrated drug development expertise, enable the Company to develop differentiated therapeutics and create value through both internal innovation and strategic partnerships.

For more information about Zymeworks, its portfolio and pipeline, visit www.zymeworks.com and follow @ZymeworksInc on X.

data.title: Immatics Presents Clinical Activity of IMA402 PRAME Bispecific and IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy across Advanced Solid Tumors in Two Oral Presentations at 2026 ESMO Annual Meeting
data.description:
• IMA402 PRAME bispecific continues to demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity in multiple indications, alongside a favorable safety profile

  • IMA402 achieved a cORR of 32%, 12.5 months median DOR and a 1-year OS rate of 91% in advanced melanoma patients with high PRAME expression

  • Clinical profile of IMA402 reinforces development path across multiple solid tumor indications, including melanoma, gynecologic cancers and lung cancer, in earlier and later treatment lines, supported by Immatics’ innovative, rapid liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing

  • IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy demonstrated deep and durable anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types with a manageable safety profile, supporting its tumor-agnostic potential. At clinically relevant dose levels in patients with advanced, heavily pretreated gynecologic cancers, cORR was 55% with a median DOR of 8.4 months

Houston, Texas and Tuebingen, Germany, October 24, 2026 – Immatics N.V. (NASDAQ: IMTX, “Immatics” or the “Company”), the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME with multiple clinical-stage programs spanning cell therapies and bispecifics, today announced updated clinical trial data from its ongoing Phase 1b study with IMA402 PRAME bispecific and its Phase 1 study with IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy.

The IMA402 data will be presented in a rapid oral presentation (1955RO) by Dirk Schadendorf, M.D., and the IMA203CD8 data were presented in an oral presentation (1946O) by Antonia Busse, M.D., at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) in Madrid, Spain. In addition, exploratory analyses of the anzu-cel Phase 1b melanoma cohort will be presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D. The slides are available in the ‘Events & Presentations’ section of the Investor & Media page on the Company’s website.

“The data presented at ESMO further underscore the potential of IMA402 as an off-the-shelf treatment option for patients with solid cancers. This promising clinical profile reinforces our strategy as we continue to advance IMA402 across multiple cancer types and treatment lines, with combination approaches further expanding its reach,” said Cedrik Britten, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer at Immatics. “In addition, as the IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy data continue to mature, we are increasingly encouraged by its broad potential for patients with advanced PRAME-positive cancers. Together with anzu-cel, IMA402 and IMA203CD8 give us three distinct and complementary approaches to target PRAME, with the potential to reach more patients across a broad range of cancers.”

Rapid Oral Presentation Summary - IMA402 PRAME TCR Bispecific Phase 1b Trial

Patient Population: Heavily pretreated patient population with a median of 3 prior lines of therapy
As of the data cutoff on June 1, 2026, 126 heavily pretreated patients across multiple tumor types, primarily melanoma and ovarian cancer, received at least one infusion of IMA402 during the dose escalation or dose expansion part of the ongoing trial (NCT05958121). Patients had received a median of 3 prior lines of systemic treatment, had a median target lesion sum of diameter of 7.4 cm and had a median of 4 tumor lesions. The efficacy population included 40 patients treated within the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) range of 10 to 45 mg across varying levels of PRAME expression. Within this population, 31 patients exhibited high PRAME expression levels (PRAME-high)1 in their tumors. Of these, all patients with PRAME-high melanoma had received prior systemic treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), with a median of 2 prior ICI regimens and all patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer were previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy.

Safety: Favorable tolerability profile as monotherapy and as combination therapy
IMA402 showed favorable tolerability across all doses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were expected, transient lymphopenia and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. No cases of ICANS were reported. No IMA402-related Grade 5 events were reported. Tolerability was consistent across all evaluated doses, including the RP2D range, with no additive toxicity observed when combined with an ICI.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: 32% cORR in PRAME-high melanoma with promising durability and survival
IMA402 showed promising anti-tumor activity as monotherapy (n=36) or in combination with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (n=4) in the efficacy population at RP2D range. Treatment with IMA402 demonstrated 10 confirmed responses resulting in an overall confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 25% (10/40) and a disease control rate (DCR) of 63% (25/40). This includes one confirmed complete response in melanoma. The longest ongoing response exceeded 2 years. In the PRAME-high population, cORR was 32% (10/31) across all indications and 32% (7/22) in patients with melanoma. The PRAME-high melanoma population further showed a median duration of response (mDOR) of 12.5 months (median follow-up, mFU, 16.8 months). Median overall survival (mOS) was not reached (mFU 8.8 months), with 91% of patients alive at 1 year (versus 60% of patients treated below RP2D range), indicating promising overall survival data irrespective of best response. Among 6 patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer, 3 confirmed responses were reported.

Next Development Steps for IMA402:
The promising clinical profile of IMA402 supports a development path across various solid tumors in earlier and later treatment lines. These include combination approaches with ICIs in melanoma and in gynecologic cancers as well as IMA402 in combination with the Company’s MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific, IMA401, in lung cancer with first data expected in 2027. Furthermore, the use of Immatics’ proprietary rapid, sensitive and reliable liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing enables precise patient selection and could support potential fast-to-market strategies, subject to regulatory approval, in PRAME-high melanoma and beyond.

Oral Presentation Summary - IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy Phase 1 Trial

Patient population: Heavily pretreated patient population with limited treatment options
As of the data cutoff on August 7, 2026, 98 heavily pretreated patients across multiple advanced solid tumor types expressing PRAME that had undergone a median of 3 prior systemic treatments were enrolled in the ongoing Phase 1 dose escalation/dose expansion trial (NCT03686124). Of these, 90 patients were evaluable for efficacy, including 27 with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer), 44 with melanoma, 12 with synovial sarcoma and 7 with other solid tumor types. All patients with ovarian cancer had received prior platinum-based therapy.

Safety: Treatment with IMA203CD8 was manageable
IMA203CD8 demonstrated a consistent and manageable safety profile across different solid tumor types and a wide dose range (median dose 1.81x109 TCR T cells, range 0.44-12.50x109). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were expected and included transient cytopenias associated with the lymphodepletion regimen and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. ICANS was infrequently observed, and no IMA203CD8-related Grade 5 events occurred. Maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was not reached with doses up to 12.5 billion IMA203CD8 cells.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: One-time infusion of IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy showed anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types
Across all evaluated dose levels and tumor types, including lower dose levels not selected for further clinical development, a one-time infusion of IMA203CD8 demonstrated an ORR of 51% (46/90) and a cORR of 41% (36/87). The DCR was 82% (74/90) and 83% (71/86) of patients with evaluable target lesions experienced tumor reduction. Responses were observed across multiple solid tumors expressing PRAME, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma, synovial sarcoma, and others. Durable long-term responses were observed with ongoing responses for more than 2.5 years.

In 20 patients with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer) treated at clinically relevant dose levels (≥DL4c), IMA203CD8 demonstrated consistent anti-tumor activity with an ORR of 60% (12/20) and a cORR of 55% (11/20), a DCR of 70% (14/20) and tumor reduction in 68% (13/19) of patients. Early durability data showed a mDOR of 8.4 months (mFU 6.0 months), a mPFS of 5.8 months (mFU 8.1 months) and mOS not reached at 7.8 months mFU.

Next Development Steps for IMA203CD8:
Phase 1a dose escalation is complete. Immatics is currently enrolling patients with uterine cancer at clinically relevant doses to further expand the clinical dataset in this indication. In addition, a Phase 1/2 investigator-initiated trial (IIT) in patients with PRAME-positive pediatric cancers is planned to start in 1H 2027. The clinical activity of IMA203CD8 observed across tumor types with distinct biology and differing levels of PRAME expression, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma and synovial sarcoma, supports the broad applicability of IMA203CD8 across PRAME-positive cancers. The development approach for IMA203CD8 will leverage targeted cohorts of selected tumor types, such as ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, rare cancers and pediatric cancers to build the clinical evidence base for broader, tumor-agnostic application.

Poster Presentation Summary – Anzu-cel Phase 1b Melanoma Cohort
Additional exploratory analyses (data cutoff Sept 24, 2025) of anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel, IMA203), presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D., demonstrated durable clinical benefit following a one-time treatment in a heavily pretreated population of patients with advanced melanoma. Durable clinical benefit was observed across patients with varied baseline clinical and treatment characteristics, with no single characteristic identified as a predictor of prolonged PFS. Exploratory analyses suggested that lower tumor burden, lower LDH, and a higher effector-to-target ratio may be associated with longer PFS. These findings further strengthen the clinical profile of anzu-cel, which is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 SUPRAME trial in advanced melanoma.

About IMA402 PRAME Bispecific
IMA402 is a molecule from Immatics’ TCR bispecifics (TCER®) pipeline directed against an HLA-A*02:01-presented peptide derived from PRAME. IMA402 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in patients with solid tumors expressing PRAME. IMA402 is part of Immatics’ strategy to leverage the full clinical potential of targeting PRAME, one of the most promising targets for TCR-based therapies.

About IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy
IMA203CD8 is Immatics’ PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Co-transduction of CD8αβ with the PRAME TCR adds functional CD4+ T cells designed to boost anti-tumor activity. IMA203CD8 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in solid tumors expressing PRAME.

About Anzu-cel PRAME Cell Therapy
Anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) is a PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Anzu-cel PRAME cell therapy is currently being evaluated in a registration-enabling randomized controlled Phase 3 trial, “SUPRAME,” in patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who have disease progression on or after treatment with at least one checkpoint inhibitor. In parallel, the Phase 1/2 clinical trial is ongoing with a focus on uveal melanoma.

About PRAME
PRAME is a tumor-associated target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Immatics’ PRAME franchise includes multiple product candidates, therapeutic modalities, indications and combination approaches: anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) and IMA203CD8, both PRAME-directed cell therapies, and IMA402, a PRAME-directed bispecific. Combination approaches include IMA402 with immune checkpoint inhibitors, IMA402 with the MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific IMA401, and anzu-cel in combination with Moderna’s PRAME mRNA therapy designed to enhance the cell therapy response.

About Immatics
Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Our cutting-edge science and robust clinical pipeline form the broadest PRAME franchise with the most PRAME indications and modalities, spanning TCR T-cell therapies and TCR bispecifics.

In the news release, DigitalXForce Scores Triple Win: IDC MarketScape Leader Recognition, Institutional Investment from Arsenal Equity Group and 514% Growth, issued 21-Oct-2026 by DigitalXForce Corporation over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that changes have been made. The complete, corrected release follows, with additional details at the end:

AI-native Enterprise TRiSCM™ innovator secures institutional backing, earns Leader recognition in GRC and Third-Party Risk Management, and accelerates global expansion

DALLAS, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DigitalXForce today announced the launch of the industry's first Enterprise TRiSCM™ (Trust, Risk, and Security Management) platform designed for the AI and Quantum era, introducing a new operating model for organizations to manage Trust, Risk, Security and Compliance through continuous assurance, operational intelligence and autonomous risk operation.

DigitalXForce, the AI-native Enterprise Trust, Risk, Security and Compliance Management (TRiSCM™) platform, today announced a strategic institutional investment from Arsenal Growth Equity to accelerate global expansion, enterprise adoption and AI-powered innovation.

The investment follows a period of exceptional momentum for DigitalXForce, highlighted by three major milestones:

  • IDC MarketScape Leader Recognition: DigitalXForce was named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Third-Party Risk Management Software 2026 Vendor Assessment (Doc #US53007725, September 2026), following its Leader positioning in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Governance, Risk, and Compliance Software Vendor Assessment, 2025 (Doc #US53615325, June 2025).
  • 514% Growth: DigitalXForce was recognized as the second fastest-growing technology company in North Texas in the 2026 Tech Titans Fast Tech Awards.
  • Strategic Institutional Investment: Arsenal Growth Equity's investment will support the company's next phase of global growth, product innovation and enterprise market expansion.

Together, these milestones reinforce DigitalXForce's evolution from an emerging GRC innovator into a rapidly scaling enterprise technology company advancing the shift toward continuous Digital Trust and AI-powered Risk Intelligence.

Institutional Investment to Accelerate Global Scale

The strategic investment from Arsenal Growth Equity will support DigitalXForce's expansion across North America, the Middle East, Europe and Asia-Pacific, while strengthening its global enterprise sales, partner ecosystem and product engineering capabilities.

The company plans to accelerate investment in its unified Enterprise TRiSCM™ platform, including Automated GRC, Continuous Control Assurance, Third-Party Risk Management, AI Risk Governance, Enterprise Security Posture Management and X-ROC™ Risk Operations.

data.description:
TOKYO, JP / ACCESS Newswire / October 24, 2026 / Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. (Nasdaq:LAWR) ("Robot Consulting" or the "Company"), a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions and legal technology, announced it has received a delisting determination from the Listing Qualifications Department (the "Staff") of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying the Company of the Staff's determination to delist the Company's American Depository Shares ("ADSs") pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rules 5101 and IM-5101-4.

The Staff's determination is based on concerns regarding historical trading activity in the Company's securities and Nasdaq's belief that certain factors may have made the Company's securities susceptible to manipulation by third parties.

Nasdaq Listing Rule IM-5101-4 allows Nasdaq "to exercise discretion to delist a company from Nasdaq based on the potential for one or more third parties to engage in misconduct impacting a company's securities where the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission] has implemented a temporary trading suspension." Nasdaq has articulated its belief that the ability for third parties to manipulate a security's price indicates that the security does not have sufficient liquidity to promote fair and orderly markets and, therefore, delisting is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.

The Company has appealed the Staff's determination to a Hearings Panel (the "Panel") on October 23, 2026. As a result of the appeal, the suspension of the Company's securities and the filing of the Form 25-NSE by Nasdaq with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") will be stayed pending the Panel's review and decision, although the existing trading halt will remain in effect unless and until it has been lifted by Nasdaq.

To date, Nasdaq has not claimed or communicated a view that there has been any wrongdoing by the Company, whether in regard to Nasdaq's investigation of the recent trading activity of the Company's securities or otherwise. The delisting determination does not have any immediate effect on the Company's ongoing business operations or financial condition, and the Company will continue to conduct its business in the ordinary course.

About Robot Consulting Co., Ltd.

Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. is a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions with an intention to expand into legal technology. data.title: Junshi Biosciences Announces Completion of First Patient Dosing in the Phase 3 Clinical Trial of JS203 in Combination with Chemotherapy for the Treatment of Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma
data.description:
SHANGHAI, China, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shanghai Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd (“Junshi Biosciences,” HKEX: 1877; SSE: 688180), a leading innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel therapies, announced that the first patient dosing has been completed in a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 3 clinical study of the company’s product, a recombinant humanized anti-CD20/CD3 bispecific antibody (code: JS203), in combination with chemotherapy compared to rituximab in combination with chemotherapy in patients with relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (R/R DLBCL) (the JS203-003-III-DLBCL Study; NCT07808827). This study is the first registrational clinical study for JS203.

DLBCL is one of the most common types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), accounting for approximately 40% of adult NHL cases in China. According to GLOBOCAN 2022 statistics, there are approximately 45,000 new cases of DLBCL in China each year, and the incidence rate shows a slow increasing trend. DLBCL is characterized by high aggressiveness and rapid progression. A retrospective study in an Asian population showed that, even after active treatment, patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL had a median overall survival (mOS) of over one year and a 5-year survival rate of approximately 30%, which necessitates the exploration of more proactive and effective treatment options.

JS203 is a recombinant humanized anti-CD20/CD3 bispecific antibody self-developed by Junshi Biosciences. It consists of anti-CD20 segment and anti-CD3 segment. By associating and activating lymphoma cells (binding to CD20) and T cells (binding to CD3), JS203 can enable T cells to kill lymphoma cells effectively.

Results from a phase 1 clinical study showed that, for JS203 monotherapy at the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) administered with step-up dosing (SUD) to 30 mg for the treatment of patients with CD20-positive relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, the objective response rate (ORR) reached 72.4%. Among patients with DLBCL, the ORR was 69.7%, and the complete response rate CRR was 39.4%, with persistent relief observed. Meanwhile, the overall safety profile was manageable, with a cytokine release syndrome (CRS) incidence rate of only 27.3% and no occurrence of immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS).

The JS203-003-III-DLBCL Study is a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 3 clinical trial, with Professor Yuqin SONG of Beijing Cancer Hospital serving as the principal investigator. It aims to compare the efficacy and safety of JS203 in combination with chemotherapy compared to rituximab in combination with chemotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The study plans to enroll 282 subjects, with overall survival (OS) as its primary endpoint. This study is the first registrational clinical study for JS203.

The JS203-003-III-DLBCL study team commented: “Early clinical studies have shown encouraging efficacy and a favorable safety profile for JS203 in combination with chemotherapy in patients with R/R DLBCL, reinforcing our confidence in the ongoing Phase 3 study. We are committed to advancing the study with rigor and efficiency, with the aim of making a new treatment option available to patients as soon as possible.”

About JS203

JS203 is a recombinant humanized anti-CD20/CD3 bispecific antibody self-developed by Junshi Biosciences. CD20 is a B lymphocyte restricted differentiation antigen and one of the most successful targets for B-cell lymphoma treatment. CD3 is an important marker on the surface of T cells, and the main mechanism of T cell engaging bispecific antibodies is using CD3 as a mediator to activate T cells to specifically attack tumor cells. JS203 consists of anti-CD20 segment and anti-CD3 segment. By associating and activating lymphoma cells (binding to CD20) and T cells (binding to CD3), JS203 can enable T cells to kill lymphoma cells effectively. To date, a Phase 3 clinical study evaluating JS203 in combination with chemotherapy versus rituximab in combination with chemotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (R/R DLBCL) is ongoing.

About Junshi Biosciences

Founded in December 2012, Junshi Biosciences (HKEX: 1877; SSE: 688180) is an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the discovery, development and commercialization of innovative therapeutics. With our outstanding capacity for innovative drug discovery, strong biotechnology R&D capability, and large-scale production capacity, we have successfully developed a drug candidate portfolio with global competitiveness and a well-structured research pipeline, which covers therapeutic areas including cancer, autoimmune, metabolic, and infectious diseases. Our innovative field spans cutting-edge therapeutic modalities, including mAbs, small-molecule drugs, ADCs, bsAb/msAb, fusion proteins, nucleic acid drugs and vaccines. Five of the company’s products have received marketing authorizations in China and international markets, one of which is toripalimab, China’s domestically developed anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. Toripalimab has been approved in over 50 countries and regions including China, the US, and Europe.

With a mission of “providing patients with world-class, trustworthy, affordable, and innovative drugs,” Junshi Biosciences is “In China, For Global.” The company currently employs more than 3,000 people worldwide. data.title: See It, Try It, Compare It: SIVP Brings CHERY’s “Technology. For Family” to Life
data.description:
WUHU, China, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- During Chery International User Summit 2026, CHERY held a family parking challenge carnival at Squirrel Town. Centred on SIVP (Super Intelligent Valet Parking), it combined a parking workshop, scenario challenges and hands-on experiences, showing global guests how intelligent parking can save families time and effort.

A Parking Technology Class Introduces SIVP as the Latest Expression of “Technology. For Family”

At the parking workshop, CHERY presented three “For Family” pillars: “Space. For Family”, “Safety. For Family” and “Technology. For Family”. Guests had experienced the first two through vehicle experiences and a crash-test challenge; SIVP brought the third to life.


CHERY Brand Director Leo Liu counted the 27 sensors on the TIGGO7 together with users on site.

CHERY’s global user research found that parking and finding a space can affect a family’s mood. In supported, mapped car parks, SIVP offers two functions: One Tap Departure lets users select a pick-up point in the app and request the vehicle to travel there; One Step Home assists with parking after users get out. Users must follow app instructions, monitor the vehicle and surroundings, and remain ready to pause or take over.

SIVP uses AI Planner and an end-to-end large model to plan movements, avoid obstacles and respond to changing situations. It marks the first large-scale overseas application of such a model in production vehicles. Its 3R11V12U1L configuration—three millimetre-wave radars, 11 high-definition cameras, 12 ultrasonic sensors and one lidar—provides 360-degree sensing, helping detect obstacles in complex parking spaces and giving families greater peace of mind.

Timed Family Challenges Compare Parking and Vehicle Pick-up

Twelve guests drew lots to form four temporary families, each playing a father, mother and child. Timed challenges compared the SIVP and control groups.

The “Monday Morning Rush” recreated the pressure of getting children ready and leaving early. Each family had to complete a sequence of tasks, including preparing breakfast, tying a tie and helping their child through breakfast, before getting into the car together. The SIVP group could summon the vehicle to the door in advance using a phone, then get straight in once the tasks were finished, avoiding a detour to collect it. The “Easier Family Shopping Challenge” recreated a supermarket trip. The SIVP group could get out and head into the shop, using the app to initiate valet parking, then summon the vehicle back after shopping. The control group had to park manually and carry their purchases back to the car park to find their vehicle. The comparison showed clearly how much time and effort could be saved when parking and collecting a car.

Hands-On Experiences Across Multiple Models Bring Family Feedback into Focus

In the open experience area, guests could visit different zones offering Automatic Parking Assist (APA) demonstrations and SIVP experiences in challenging spaces, including bays at the end of dead-end parking aisles and extremely narrow bays. These activities showcased SIVP’s ability to handle complex parking scenarios. Afterwards, guests completed questionnaires about their experiences. Their feedback will inform ongoing improvements to SIVP, bringing intelligent parking technology closer to families’ actual mobility needs.

From technical explanations in the classroom and clear comparisons in the challenges to hands-on operation in the experience area, the carnival demonstrated CHERY’s understanding of families through the everyday act of parking. Parking need no longer be a burden on family outings, and every minute saved can be spent with loved ones. Through SIVP, “Technology. For Family” is becoming part of daily life for more families.

Slate Grocery REIT (TSX: SGR.U) (TSX: SGR.UN) (the “REIT”), an owner and operator of U.S. grocery-anchored real estate, announced today that it has obtained an interim order (the “Interim Order”) of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) (the “Court”) in connection with the proposed acquisition by EP/BRX Holdings LLC (the “Purchaser”), a joint venture between an affiliate of Brixmor Property Group Inc. and affiliates of Everview Partners, L.P., of all of the REIT’s issued and outstanding units pursuant to the terms and conditions of an arrangement agreement (the “Arrangement Agreement”) among the REIT, the Purchaser and 1001700324 Ontario Inc. dated September 27, 2026 (the “Arrangement”). The Arrangement was previously announced by the REIT on September 28, 2026.

Interim Order, Meeting and Circular

The Interim Order, granted on October 22, 2026, authorizes the calling and holding of a special meeting of unitholders of the REIT (the “Meeting”) to consider and vote on a special resolution approving the Arrangement. The Meeting is scheduled to be held in a virtual-only format on Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Eastern time). Unitholders of record as of the close of business on October 20, 2026 will be entitled to receive notice of and vote at the Meeting.

The REIT expects to file its management information circular (the “Circular”) and related meeting materials on SEDAR+ on November 2, 2026 and to mail those materials to unitholders on or about November 2, 2026. The Circular will provide details of the Arrangement, the matters to be considered at the Meeting and the procedures for participating in and voting at the Meeting. Once filed, the Circular and related meeting materials will be available under the REIT’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the REIT’s website at slategroceryreit.com. Unitholders are urged to read the Circular and related meeting materials carefully when they become available.

Other Matters

In connection with the Arrangement, the REIT has applied to the Ontario Securities Commission (the “OSC”) for discretionary exemptive relief from the requirement to obtain minority approval on a class-by-class basis under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”) with a view to ensuring that the vote is structured in a manner that is fair to all unitholders. Under the REIT’s declaration of trust, holders of class A units, class I units and class U units generally vote together as a single class unless the business to be transacted affects holders of one class in a manner materially different from its effect on holders of another class. The REIT’s board of trustees has determined that the Arrangement does not have such a differential effect.

If the requested relief is granted, disinterested holders of class A units, class I units and class U units will vote on the Arrangement under MI 61-101 together as a single class, with one vote per unit, rather than separately by class. Votes required to be excluded under MI 61-101 will be excluded from that minority approval vote. There can be no assurance that the requested relief will be granted by the OSC.

The REIT’s declaration of trust permits the trustees of the REIT to require the conversion of all outstanding class A units or class I units into class U units if the number of outstanding units of the applicable class is less than 10% of the number of units of that class issued on the closing of the REIT’s initial public offering, which is currently the case for both the class A units and class I units. If the requested relief is not secured prior to the date that is 10 business days before the Meeting, all class A units and class I units will be converted into class U units, effective before the Meeting, pursuant to such provisions. Holders of class A units or class I units on the record date whose units are so converted will be deemed to have held those class U units on the record date, the whole in accordance with the terms of the REIT’s declaration of trust.

Completion of the Arrangement remains subject to the requisite unitholder approvals, including approval by at least two-thirds of the votes cast by unitholders voting together as a single class and the applicable minority approval under MI 61-101, receipt of the final order of the Court approving the Arrangement, receipt of the required approval under the Investment Canada Act, and the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions to closing set out in the Arrangement Agreement. Subject to obtaining the necessary approvals and satisfying or waiving the other closing conditions, the Arrangement is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

It's exciting to see these celebrations grow year after year, alongside the impact of our work with school systems across California," said Think Education Founder and CEO Randy Barth. "Together, we're helping hundreds of thousands of students access opportunities to build skills beyond the traditional school day and Lights On Afterschool is a chance to recognize the people and partnerships that make that possible."

Lunit and Summit Therapeutics Announce Agreement to Apply AI-powered SCOPE IO Platform for Tumor Microenvironment Analysis in Immuno-Oncology Development

Lunit and Summit Therapeutics Announce Agreement to Apply AI-powered SCOPE IO Platform for Tumor Microenvironment Analysis in Immuno-Oncology Development

PR Newswire

SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 24, 2026

Research Will Use Lunit's AI-powered Pathology Platform to Analyze H&E Whole-Slide Images and Generate Scalable Insights into Tumor Microenvironment Biology

SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lunit Inc. (KRX: 328130) and Summit Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: SMMT) today announced a research agreement to evaluate the use of Lunit SCOPE IO, Lunit's AI-powered pathology platform, for tumor microenvironment analysis in support of Summit's immuno-oncology development programs with ivonescimab.

The effort will focus on applying Lunit SCOPE IO to hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) whole-slide images to characterize tumor microenvironment features. The companies aim to explore how AI-powered pathology analysis can support biomarker discovery, patient stratification or selection, and a deeper biological understanding of response to ivonescimab therapies.

Summit is developing ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class investigational PD-1 / VEGF bispecific antibody, in several solid tumors. Lunit SCOPE IO is designed to support immuno-oncology research and biomarker development through AI-powered analysis of H&E slides, enabling scalable assessment of tumor microenvironment features without requiring additional stains or assays.

"Understanding the tumor microenvironment is increasingly important as immuno-oncology moves beyond single-axis checkpoint inhibition toward more complex mechanisms and combinations," said Allen Yang, MD, PhD, Chief Research and Development Strategy Officer of Summit. "We are pleased to work with Lunit to explore how AI-powered pathology can help generate deeper, more scalable insights from routine tissue samples and inform the continued development of ivonescimab."

"Summit is at the forefront of next-generation immuno-oncology development, and we are excited to support its efforts with Lunit SCOPE IO," said Brandon Suh, Lunit CEO. "By extracting quantitative, spatially resolved immune and tumor microenvironment features from standard H&E slides, we believe SCOPE IO can help biopharma partners better understand which patients may benefit from immuno-oncology therapies and why."

This agreement reflects the growing importance of computational pathology in oncology drug development. Routine H&E slides contain rich information about tumor architecture, immune infiltration, stromal organization, and spatial interactions within the tumor microenvironment. However, traditional manual assessment can be difficult to scale and may not fully capture the quantitative and spatial complexity of the tumor-immune interface. AI-powered analysis offers the potential to convert these routinely generated pathology images into reproducible, high-dimensional biomarker data.

The companies expect the work to generate tumor microenvironment insights that may inform future translational research, exploratory biomarker strategies, and clinical development planning. No clinical outcome data are being announced as part of this release.

 *Lunit SCOPE products are for research use only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures or decisions.

About Ivonescimab

Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit's license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit's license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF.

This design is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab's specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of ivonescimab's design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets.

Ivonescimab was invented by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 5,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally and over 100,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso.

There are currently 17 Phase III clinical studies that are either announced, ongoing, or have been completed studying ivonescimab, five of which are Summit-sponsored global studies, two of which are studies sponsored by cooperative groups, and 10 of which are being or have been conducted in China by Akeso. Summit began its clinical development of ivonescimab in NSCLC (HARMONi, HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7) and expanded its sponsored Phase III clinical development program into colorectal cancer (CRC; HARMONi-GI3) and urothelial carcinoma (bladder cancer; HARMONi-GU1). The two cooperative studies are in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC; ILLUMINE) and biliary tract cancer (BTC; EA2251).

Five Phase III ivonescimab clinical trials have read out to date, all five with positive data. Four of these five studies are in NSCLC and one is in BTC. In addition to Summit's positive HARMONi study in NSCLC, Akeso has had positive read-outs in four single-region (China), randomized Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi-A, HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6 (each in NSCLC), and HARMONi-GI1 (in BTC) for ivonescimab, including a statistically significant overall survival benefit in all four studies from China.

Akeso is actively conducting additional Phase III clinical studies in settings outside of NSCLC and biliary-tract cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit's license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024.

About Lunit

Founded in 2013, Lunit (KRX: 328130) is a global leader on a mission to conquer cancer through AI. Our clinically validated solutions span medical imaging, breast health, and biomarker analysis, empowering earlier detection, smarter treatment decisions, and more precise outcomes across the cancer care continuum.

Lunit offers a comprehensive suite spanning risk prediction and early detection to precision oncology. Our FDA-cleared Lunit INSIGHT Breast Suite and breast health solutions support cancer screening in thousands of medical institutions worldwide, while the Lunit SCOPE platform is used in research partnership with global pharma and laboratory leaders for biomarker research, and companion diagnostic development.

Trusted by over 10,000 sites in more than 65 countries, Lunit combines deep medical expertise with continuously evolving datasets to deliver measurable impact for patients, clinicians, and researchers alike. Headquartered in Seoul with global offices, Lunit is driving the worldwide fight against cancer. Learn more at lunit.io.

About Summit Therapeutics Inc.

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs.

Summit was founded in 2003 and the company's shares are listed on the Nasdaq Global Market (symbol "SMMT"). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, with additional offices in Palo Alto, California, Princeton, New Jersey, Dublin, Ireland, and Oxford, UK.

For more information, please visit https://www.smmttx.com and follow Summit on X @SMMT_TX.
